title: Tansy and Little Bear's Moon-Milk Mission
markdown:
In a little cottage tucked beside a Whispering Willow lived a kitten named Tansy. She was as soft as a dandelion puff, and her whiskers twitched with a thousand wiggly thoughts. Her fur was the colour of warm honey. When she purred, it sounded like a tiny happy tune bubbling up.

Right beside her, always, was Little Bear Blue. He was a most comforting bear, fur the colour of a summer sky, eyes like shiny black buttons that always seemed to twinkle. When he was happy, a deep gentle rumble started in his chest, like a little engine humming a lullaby.

One evening, as the moon began to spill silvery light through the windowpanes, Tansy felt a tickle in her whiskers. The kind of tickle that meant something kind was about to happen.

“Little Bear Blue,” she purred, tail giving a happy flick. “Did you know the attic mice get thirsty too? They live all the way up there, and sometimes the dew is a bit too far to reach.”

Little Bear Blue gave a soft rumbling hum. “Indeed. I’ve often wondered about them. The moonbeams make the most delicious moon-milk, but it’s very high up for the little mice to get their own.” He sighed, and the sigh puffed out his soft chest.

“Ah, but here’s the thing.” Tansy nudged a little china cup with her paw. It was smaller than her smallest paw print and had painted bluebells all around its rim. It shimmered faintly, as if it had already caught some of the moon’s light. “This teacup is just the right size for thirsty little mice.”

Little Bear Blue nodded, head bobbing. “A splendid idea. A mouse-pleasing plan. But how will we get it upstairs? The stairs are so… long.” He wiggled his plush paws, which looked quite big and clumsy next to the tiny cup. “And quite a trek for us.”

Tansy tilted her head, ears perked. “We’ll carry it together. You’ll hold it steady, like a little boat on a calm sea, and I’ll keep it balanced with my nose. And when we get to the top, we’ll share it with the attic mice. They’ll be ever so pleased.”

She sang, very softly:

Up the stairs we go,
for the thirsty attic mice.

And so, with the tiny teacup cradled between them — Little Bear Blue holding it with sturdy paws, Tansy nudging it ever so gently with her soft nose — they began their journey. The stairs were indeed long, winding up, up, up toward the roof. The teacup wobbled a tiny bit with each step. Tansy’s heart gave a little flutter, like a butterfly’s wing. She did not like it when precious moon-milk wobbled too much.

“Oh dear. It’s a bit wobbly.”

Little Bear Blue’s button eyes looked down, brow furrowed. “It’s a bit tricky. The teacup is so delicate, and my paws are so… round. They don’t have little pointy bits to hold on just so.” He almost let it slip.

Tansy stretched out a paw, soft pads brushing the cool china. “Let me help.” She gently nudged the side of the cup. Together, with his steady grip and her gentle nudges, they made their way up.

Up the stairs we go,
for the thirsty attic mice.

Past the big sleepy armchair where Grandpa sometimes napped. Past the framed picture of the slightly grumpy-looking cat who lived next door. The air grew a little cooler. They could smell the faint sweet scent of old wood. The wooden stairs creaked a little lullaby under their paws.

They reached the top landing. The attic door was slightly ajar, and a sliver of moonlight, like a pale golden smile, peeked from the gap. Tansy and Little Bear Blue pushed it open with a soft whispery creak.

Inside it was not dark and scary at all. It was filled with soft dusty moonlight, the faint scent of old paper, and the quiet whisper of tiny paws. Little scurrying shadows turned out to be the attic mice, whiskers twitching with happy expectation, tiny noses sniffing the air. They were all gathered, waiting.

“We brought moon-milk,” Tansy announced, a soft happy meow that echoed slightly.

The mice squeaked with delight, a chorus of happy little sounds. One mouse with particularly long wobbly whiskers scurried forward, paws pattering on the wood. “Thank you, Tansy. Thank you, Little Bear Blue. We were so thirsty, and the moonbeams are so high.”

Carefully, with a gentle tilt from Tansy and a steady hold from Little Bear Blue, they tipped the teacup. A little stream of silvery moon-milk poured out, catching the light and sparkling like a tiny river of starlight. Each mouse took a tiny delicate sip. Noses wiggled. Eyes shone brighter.

“This is the best moon-milk ever,” chirped another mouse, already licking his whiskers.

Tansy and Little Bear Blue sat down on a soft dusty rug that felt like a cloud, watching the happy mice. The teacup was empty, but their hearts were wonderfully full. The moonlight made the attic feel cozy and safe.

“That was a bit wobbly, wasn’t it?” Tansy purred, looking back toward the stairs with a happy little sigh.

Little Bear Blue rumbled contentedly. “But we did it. And it was worth it.” He nudged her gently, and she nuzzled him back, her soft fur tickling his sky-blue cheek.

The attic mice chirped their thanks again, little voices like tinkling bells. And in that quiet moonlit attic, a gentle adventure found its perfectly sweet, very cozy end.
characters: Tansy (a kitten), Little Bear Blue (a plush bear)
